Ao final da aula você consegue:
resolver oito itens justificando exclusão de opções.
O professor lê; o aluno diz a paráfrase:
NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER
“Some people think it's about cost, but actually it's about time.”
“My tutor suggested X, but I prefer Y.”
Verdadeiro, mas não responde à pergunta:
the key factor / what really matters
let down / not what I expected
Palavras de contraste (sinal de que a resposta vem depois!)
but · however · actually · in fact · although · the thing is · what surprised me was
It WASN'T the price, it was the LOCATION.
Some people think it's the price, but actually what really matters is the location.

explanations.general: Correct answer: It's too expensive for us.
Correct answer: I don't really like it.

questions.questionText: Which word usually signals that the real answer is coming?
“It's a bit of a trek” means it's quite ______. (longe)

What was the problem with the first hotel?
A) It was noisy. B) It was far from the centre. C) It was expensive.
“The first hotel was actually quite reasonable, and it was right in the centre. But the street was full of bars, so we hardly slept at all.”
What does the woman want to do next year?
A) travel B) study C) work
“I thought about travelling for a while, but I've decided I really need to save money, so I'm going to get a full-time job — maybe I'll do a master's later.”
What did the speaker find most surprising about the city?
A) the weather B) the food C) the people
“I expected the rain — everyone warns you about that. The food was good, as I'd heard. What I didn't expect was how friendly everyone was — strangers would just start chatting to you.”

content.text: leia a conversa uma vez. Dê 1 minuto para o aluno ler as perguntas antes.
dois estudantes, Mia e Josh, falam sobre um projeto de pesquisa de campo.
Why did they choose the river as their study site?
A) It's close to the university. B) Their tutor recommended it. C) It has a lot of wildlife.
What was the main problem on the first visit?
A) bad weather B) broken equipment C) getting lost
What does Josh think about the data so far?
A) It's very reliable. B) The sample is too small. C) It contradicts previous studies.
What will they do next week?
A) visit the river again B) meet their tutor C) start writing the report
So, how do you think the project's going?
Not bad. I'm glad we went for the river. I know Dr. Lewis suggested the woodland, but the river's only ten minutes from campus by bike.
True, and it's not like the woodland has more animals anyway.
Exactly. The first visit was a bit of a disaster, though.
Well, the rain didn't help, but we'd have been fine if the water-testing kit hadn't stopped working after twenty minutes.
Right. And we didn't get lost at all, thanks to my map!
Ha, yes. As for the results, I'm a bit worried. They look consistent, but we've only got samples from three days. That's not enough to say anything for sure.
Do they agree with what other studies found?
More or less, yes. So, next week — should we go back to the river?
I think we should see Dr. Lewis first and ask how many more samples we need. Then we can plan more visits.
OK, I'll email her to set up a meeting. The report can wait till we've got more data.
